message.content:
Research COMPANIES for cold outreach, not job postings. Return data only, no commentary.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Prabhavit Gupta, Venice, Italy. Indian passport with an Italian EU long-term residence permit, so he can work across most of the EU with no sponsorship (Ireland and Denmark opted out; the UK, Switzerland and the US need sponsorship, so skip companies that only hire or contract there). ~3 years experience.
At FlowSpace, a coworking booking platform grown 2,000 to 4,500+ users, he owned the acquisition and activation plumbing: lead capture consolidated into the CRM with enrichment, outbound and sales-funnel automation, AI support agents, and a scraping and parsing pipeline that grew listings supply. He is an engineer who also owned product.
Stack: n8n (deep), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, HubSpot-style CRM automation, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate (certified).
English only. Targets EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200/day as an Italian sole trader with an individual Partita IVA (no limited company).

TWO OUTREACH MODES, tag every company with one or both:
- "speculative job": a direct approach could create or surface a role.
- "freelance client": they would plausibly BUY GTM engineering or automation work at around EUR 200 a day, including subcontracting when they have more client work than builders.

YOUR LANE: go-to-market engineering and revenue operations as a service, in Europe. Cover:
- GTM engineering agencies and "outbound as a service" shops in the EU that build Clay, HubSpot, Apollo, Smartlead and n8n stacks for clients.
- RevOps consultancies and HubSpot Solutions Partners in the EU, especially Diamond and Platinum tier partners who work in English.
- Lifecycle and marketing-automation agencies in the EU (Customer.io, Braze, Klaviyo, Iterable partners).
- Demand-generation and growth agencies in Europe that publicly sell automation and AI workflow builds rather than only media buying.
- B2B SaaS scale-ups in the EU that have visibly grown their sales team but have no automation or RevOps engineer, since that is the classic unfilled gap he can name in a first message.
Prioritise agencies small enough that a founder or head of delivery reads inbound.

FOR EACH COMPANY RETURN
- what they actually do, in one line
- the SPECIFIC reason he is unusual for them: he is an engineer who has run the funnel plumbing end to end rather than a marketer who can use Zapier, he built enrichment into the CRM, and he can ship the app around the automation. Tie it to something real. Generic praise is useless.
- the best route in. He will reach people on LinkedIn, so give the exact JOB TITLE to search for at that company plus the company's LinkedIn page URL. Name a specific person ONLY if their name and role are publicly published on the company's own site, a partner directory or a press page, and say where you saw it. NEVER invent or guess an email address or a person. If the company publishes a general contact email on its own website, include it verbatim.
- what he should lead with in the first message, one sentence, concrete.
- watch-outs: language requirements, whether the work is US-hours, whether they need a limited company rather than a sole trader, whether they look dormant.

RULES
- Companies must currently exist and be active. Check.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Never invent a URL, a person, an email or a funding figure. If you do not know, write "not stated".
- Do NOT return these, already covered as live job leads: GTM Base, SalesCaptain, Huzzle, Wing Assistant, Paires, Sophie.camp, Growth Today, Swans, 10x.Team, Oryn Group, Lleverage, peopleIX, salesHAX.

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON array, no prose before or after:
{"company":"","what":"","hq":"","size":"","mode":"speculative job|freelance client|both","why_him":"","route_in":"","linkedin":"","public_email":"","lead_with":"","watch_outs":"","source":""}
Aim for 14 to 18 companies.
